text:
alex: Quick follow-up from the RFC — we need a concrete decision on 'priority lifetimes' for ingested telemetry. proposal attached in thread below, TL;DR: short-lived high-priority markers we can honor for routing/retention; then fall back to standard sampling after TTL expires.

maria: +1 on TTLs, but need to be explicit about semantics: is TTL per-event or per-session/trace?

alex: per-event by default. we can offer a session-level override via trace_id binding (opt-in). keeping per-event keeps semantics simple for cost accounting.

cheng: cost concern: if teams mark lots of events high-priority with long TTLs, retention/cost explode. we should enforce a global max-ttl and a per-tenant burn rate.

sam: Agreed. propose: default high-priority-ttl = 30s, max-ttl = 24h for enterprise tenants only, plus a tokens-per-tenant budget. if you go over budget, priority downgrades and we tag reason.

maria: How does downgrade interact with sampling and query results? we need deterministic labeling so analytics don't silently change.

alex: downgrade must add an annotation "priority_downgraded=budget_exhausted" and preserve original requested priority in metadata. downstream agents and queries can choose to filter or include.

taylor: operationally, where do we check TTLs? at edge collector? at the ingestion router? doing it at the edge reduces load but makes enforcement harder for cross-region traces.

cheng: prefer enforcement at gateway/edge for fast routing decisions (hot path), and a stale-check at central ingress that can correct missed downgrades. two-phase enforcement.

sam: what about late enrichment? if enrichment happens after TTL expiry, do we retroactively reclassify or keep the classification at ingest time?

alex: classification is immutable at ingest time for routing and immediate retention decisions. enrichment can add attributes but can't increase retention tier. it can, however, trigger a manual reclassify workflow for SRE/owner review (audit trail required).

maria: we'll need clear docs and UI signals in Console: token burn rate, remaining budget, sample-rate impact. ops must be able to toggle emergency overrides.

taylor: Implementation notes: add a small per-tenant token bucket in the ingest-controller with a cheap memcached fallback for Dedicated. policy decision time is sub-ms.

cheng: Also, telemetry aggregation paths (fanout -> compactor -> long-term store) need contract: the compactor must keep "priority_ttl_expiry" on envelope until it's safe to evict. otherwise chargeback will be wrong.

sam: Can we represent TTL as epoch (expiry_ts) instead of delta? fewer edge math bugs. store expiry_ts in envelope headers.

alex: +1 epoch expiry_ts. default = now + 30s. include both fields in debug logging for sanity.

ingest-bot: test-notice: added unit tests for token-bucket + ttl expiry in CI pipeline (PR: #7821). :white_check_mark:

maria: Action items: 1) ops/console UX ticket for token visibility (maria) 2) ingest-controller prototype for token-bucket + ttl enforcement (taylor/cheng) 3) docs + semantics page + alerting guidance (alex) 4) add audit trail for downgrades (sam).

alex: timeline: prototype this week, internal canary next week. any blockers?

taylor: no blockers on infra side, but need final max-ttl policy from product/legal for regulated customers.

maria: I'll sync with product/legal today.

alex: ok, i'll open a short RFC addendum with concrete fields (expiry_ts, requested_priority, downgraded_flag, downgrade_reason) and a sample envelope. will ping for reviews.

cheng: Nits: make sure GDPR data-retention rules can't be bypassed by priority. priority should only affect routing/retention tier, not retention beyond legal minima.

alex: absolutely. add to RFC addendum.

sam: sounding good. will track PR and test matrix (sampling + enrichment + downgrade combos).

maria: thanks all.
